deck.section_name: 29. An Introduction to A Level Organic Chemistry
deck.title: Formulas, Functional Groups & the Naming of Organic Compounds

front_blocks.md: Define **functional group**.

back_blocks.md: A **functional group** is an atom or group of atoms in an organic molecule that determines its characteristic chemical and physical properties.

cards.front_md: Define **functional group**.
cards.back_md: A **functional group** is an atom or group of atoms in an organic molecule that determines its characteristic chemical and physical properties.

front_blocks.md: Why do arenes prefer substitution reactions over addition reactions?

back_blocks.md: Arenes prefer substitution reactions because the delocalised π electron ring system is extremely stable. Addition reactions would disrupt this **aromatic stabilisation**, whereas substitution reactions maintain the delocalised ring.

cards.front_md: Why do arenes prefer substitution reactions over addition reactions?
cards.back_md: Arenes prefer substitution reactions because the delocalised π electron ring system is extremely stable. Addition reactions would disrupt this **aromatic stabilisation**, whereas substitution reactions maintain the delocalised ring.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Halogenoarenes are soluble in water due to the halogen atom attached to the ring.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Halogenoarenes are insoluble in water. The non-polar hydrocarbon ring means it is not energetically favourable for halogenoarene molecules to break the hydrogen bonds between water molecules.

front_blocks.md: Amines are basic due to the **..........** on the nitrogen atom, which can accept a proton.

back_blocks.md: Amines are basic due to the **lone pair of electrons** on the nitrogen atom, which can accept a proton.

cards.front_md: Amines are basic due to the **..........** on the nitrogen atom, which can accept a proton.
cards.back_md: Amines are basic due to the **lone pair of electrons** on the nitrogen atom, which can accept a proton.

front_blocks.md: Define **phenol**.

back_blocks.md: A **phenol** is an aromatic compound containing a hydroxyl group (–OH) bonded directly to a benzene ring.

cards.front_md: Define **phenol**.
cards.back_md: A **phenol** is an aromatic compound containing a hydroxyl group (–OH) bonded directly to a benzene ring.

front_blocks.md: Why is the –OH group in phenol more acidic than in alcohols?

back_blocks.md: The oxygen in phenol donates one of its **lone pairs** into the ring's π system, increasing electron density in the ring. This weakens the **O–H bond**, making the hydrogen easier to donate and phenol more acidic than an alcohol.

cards.front_md: Why is the –OH group in phenol more acidic than in alcohols?
cards.back_md: The oxygen in phenol donates one of its **lone pairs** into the ring's π system, increasing electron density in the ring. This weakens the **O–H bond**, making the hydrogen easier to donate and phenol more acidic than an alcohol.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Amides are more basic than amines.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Amides are less basic than amines because the lone pair on the nitrogen is delocalised into the adjacent C=O group, making it less available to accept a proton.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Amides are more basic than amines.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Amides are less basic than amines because the lone pair on the nitrogen is delocalised into the adjacent C=O group, making it less available to accept a proton.

front_blocks.md: Acyl chlorides are extremely reactive and readily undergo **..........** reactions in which the chlorine atom is replaced by another species.

back_blocks.md: Acyl chlorides are extremely reactive and readily undergo **substitution** reactions in which the chlorine atom is replaced by another species.

cards.front_md: Acyl chlorides are extremely reactive and readily undergo **..........** reactions in which the chlorine atom is replaced by another species.
cards.back_md: Acyl chlorides are extremely reactive and readily undergo **substitution** reactions in which the chlorine atom is replaced by another species.

front_blocks.md: What structural features define an amino acid?

back_blocks.md: An amino acid contains both an **amine group** (–NH<sub>2</sub>) and a **carboxyl group** (–COOH). Most amino acids have a chiral centre and exhibit optical isomers, except for glycine.

cards.front_md: What structural features define an amino acid?
cards.back_md: An amino acid contains both an **amine group** (–NH<sub>2</sub>) and a **carboxyl group** (–COOH). Most amino acids have a chiral centre and exhibit optical isomers, except for glycine.

front_blocks.md: Define **skeletal formula**.

back_blocks.md: A **skeletal formula** is a simplified structural representation of an organic molecule that shows the carbon skeleton as a zigzag, with functional groups shown explicitly and hydrogen atoms on carbon omitted.

cards.front_md: Define **skeletal formula**.
cards.back_md: A **skeletal formula** is a simplified structural representation of an organic molecule that shows the carbon skeleton as a zigzag, with functional groups shown explicitly and hydrogen atoms on carbon omitted.

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between a structural formula and a displayed formula?

back_blocks.md: A **structural formula** shows how atoms are grouped and bonded without showing all individual bonds. A **displayed formula** shows every bond in the molecule explicitly, including all C–H bonds.

cards.front_md: What is the difference between a structural formula and a displayed formula?
cards.back_md: A **structural formula** shows how atoms are grouped and bonded without showing all individual bonds. A **displayed formula** shows every bond in the molecule explicitly, including all C–H bonds.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A general formula can be used to represent all members of a homologous series.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
A general formula gives the simplest algebraic expression for any member of a homologous series. For example, alkanes have the general formula C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub>.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

**True.**

front_blocks.md: In a skeletal formula, carbon atoms are represented by **..........** in a zigzag chain, and hydrogen atoms bonded to carbon are **..........** .

back_blocks.md: In a skeletal formula, carbon atoms are represented by **vertices/line ends** in a zigzag chain, and hydrogen atoms bonded to carbon are **not shown**.

cards.front_md: In a skeletal formula, carbon atoms are represented by **..........** in a zigzag chain, and hydrogen atoms bonded to carbon are **..........** .
cards.back_md: In a skeletal formula, carbon atoms are represented by **vertices/line ends** in a zigzag chain, and hydrogen atoms bonded to carbon are **not shown**.

front_blocks.md: Define **general formula**.

back_blocks.md: A **general formula** is the simplest algebraic expression that describes the molecular formula of any member of a homologous series.

cards.front_md: Define **general formula**.
cards.back_md: A **general formula** is the simplest algebraic expression that describes the molecular formula of any member of a homologous series.

front_blocks.md: Which type of formula shows every atom and bond in a molecule?

back_blocks.md: A displayed formula shows **every atom and every bond** in the molecule, including all C–H bonds.

cards.front_md: Which type of formula shows every atom and bond in a molecule?
cards.back_md: A displayed formula shows **every atom and every bond** in the molecule, including all C–H bonds.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A structural formula shows all individual C–H bonds explicitly.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
A structural formula groups atoms together (e.g. CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>OH) without drawing every individual bond. It is the displayed formula that shows all bonds explicitly.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

A structural formula shows all individual C–H bonds explicitly.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

A structural formula groups atoms together (e.g. CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>OH) without drawing every individual bond. It is the displayed formula that shows all bonds explicitly.

front_blocks.md: The four types of formula used for organic compounds are: general formula, **..........**  , displayed formula and skeletal formula.

back_blocks.md: The four types of formula used for organic compounds are: general formula, **structural formula**, displayed formula and skeletal formula.

cards.front_md: The four types of formula used for organic compounds are: general formula, **..........**  , displayed formula and skeletal formula.
cards.back_md: The four types of formula used for organic compounds are: general formula, **structural formula**, displayed formula and skeletal formula.

front_blocks.md: Why are skeletal formulae particularly useful for complex organic molecules?

back_blocks.md: Skeletal formulae are useful for complex molecules because they omit carbon and hydrogen atoms on the chain, making the structure cleaner and easier to read. **Functional groups and heteroatoms** are still shown explicitly.

cards.front_md: Why are skeletal formulae particularly useful for complex organic molecules?
cards.back_md: Skeletal formulae are useful for complex molecules because they omit carbon and hydrogen atoms on the chain, making the structure cleaner and easier to read. **Functional groups and heteroatoms** are still shown explicitly.

front_blocks.md: Define **systematic nomenclature**.

back_blocks.md: A **systematic nomenclature** is a standardised method of naming organic compounds based on the length of the longest carbon chain, the functional group present and the positions of substituents.

cards.front_md: Define **systematic nomenclature**.
cards.back_md: A **systematic nomenclature** is a standardised method of naming organic compounds based on the length of the longest carbon chain, the functional group present and the positions of substituents.

front_blocks.md: What is the first step when naming an aliphatic organic compound systematically?

back_blocks.md: Identify the **longest carbon chain** that contains the **principal functional group**. This gives the parent chain name and the base suffix.

cards.front_md: What is the first step when naming an aliphatic organic compound systematically?
cards.back_md: Identify the **longest carbon chain** that contains the **principal functional group**. This gives the parent chain name and the base suffix.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
When numbering the carbon chain, the functional group should be given the highest possible locant.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
The carbon chain should be numbered so that the principal functional group has the **lowest** possible locant.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

When numbering the carbon chain, the functional group should be given the highest possible locant.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

The carbon chain should be numbered so that the principal functional group has the **lowest** possible locant.

front_blocks.md: When two or more identical substituents are present, the prefixes **..........**  , tri- or tetra- are added before the substituent name.

back_blocks.md: When two or more identical substituents are present, the prefixes **di-**, tri- or tetra- are added before the substituent name.

cards.front_md: When two or more identical substituents are present, the prefixes **..........**  , tri- or tetra- are added before the substituent name.

front_blocks.md: Define **aromatic compound**.

back_blocks.md: An **aromatic compound** is an organic compound that contains a benzene ring with a conjugated π system of delocalised electrons.

cards.front_md: Define **aromatic compound**.
cards.back_md: An **aromatic compound** is an organic compound that contains a benzene ring with a conjugated π system of delocalised electrons.

front_blocks.md: How is the naming of aromatic compounds similar to that of aliphatic compounds?

back_blocks.md: Both use the position numbering system to indicate where substituents are located. For aromatic compounds, benzene is the parent name and substituents are numbered to give the **lowest possible locants**.

cards.front_md: How is the naming of aromatic compounds similar to that of aliphatic compounds?
cards.back_md: Both use the position numbering system to indicate where substituents are located. For aromatic compounds, benzene is the parent name and substituents are numbered to give the **lowest possible locants**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Multiple substituents on a benzene ring are listed alphabetically before the parent name.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Substituents on a benzene ring (and on aliphatic chains) are listed as prefixes in alphabetical order before the parent chain name.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Multiple substituents on a benzene ring are listed alphabetically before the parent name.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

Substituents on a benzene ring (and on aliphatic chains) are listed as prefixes in alphabetical order before the parent chain name.

front_blocks.md: In 2-methylchlorobenzene, the number 2 indicates the position of the **..........** group relative to the **..........** group.

back_blocks.md: In 2-methylchlorobenzene, the number 2 indicates the position of the **methyl** group relative to the **chloro** group.

cards.front_md: In 2-methylchlorobenzene, the number 2 indicates the position of the **..........** group relative to the **..........** group.
cards.back_md: In 2-methylchlorobenzene, the number 2 indicates the position of the **methyl** group relative to the **chloro** group.

front_blocks.md: What suffix is used in the name of an amide, and what functional group does it indicate?

back_blocks.md: The suffix **-amide** is used. It indicates the presence of the –CONH<sub>2</sub> group, which contains a carbonyl (C=O) and an amine (–NH<sub>2</sub>) group.
